android.extraProguardRules:
# @stripe/stripe-react-native ships no consumer rules; its bridge
# classes are reached reflectively from JS.
-keep class com.reactnativestripesdk.** { *; }

# Expo resolves modules by name at runtime.
-keep class * extends expo.modules.kotlin.modules.Module { *; }
-keep class * implements expo.modules.core.interfaces.Package { *; }

# Stripe's Issuing push-provisioning classes live in a separate
# optional artifact that is not a dependency here, and nothing
# calls that path (enableGooglePay is false).
-dontwarn com.stripe.android.pushProvisioning.**

# @react-native-google-signin ships no consumer rules, and registers through a
# classic ReactPackage rather than as an Expo module, so the rule above does
# not cover it. A stripped native module is a release-only failure: it works in
# debug and throws "module not found" in the APK people install.
-keep class com.reactnativegooglesignin.** { *; }
